title: Method-shape: free fn reassemble() (uu-multi) vs method finish() (yenc-multi)
description:
## Finding

The terminal reassembly operation uses a different calling convention across the two multi-part crates:

- uuencoding-multi: pub fn reassemble(collection: &PartCollection) -> Result<ReassembledFile, MultiUuError>
  - Free function; takes a shared reference; PartCollection remains usable after.
- yencoding-multi: pub fn finish(self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AssemblyError>
  - Consuming method; Assembler is destroyed; no inspection after finish().

## Impact

A caller writing generic code over both formats (e.g. a trait or macro) cannot unify the call pattern. The consuming-vs-borrowing difference has semantic consequences: with uuencoding-multi the caller can inspect the PartCollection after reassembly (e.g. to check missing_parts); with yencoding-multi the Assembler is gone after finish(). This asymmetry is not required by the protocols — the yEncoding assembler could equally return a struct containing the buffer and expose missing_ranges() before consumption.
close_reason: reassemble() (free fn) vs finish() (method) reflects different design patterns appropriate to each crate. uuencoding-multi assembles in one shot from a complete collection; yencoding-multi streams parts incrementally. Harmonizing would mean changing one crate's API to match a pattern that doesn't fit its use case.
